Strike Halts Production at Major Electrical Equipment Plants Across India

A nationwide strike by electrical equipment workers has entered its second day, disrupting operations at several major manufacturing hubs across India. Thousands of workers, represented by the All-India Electrical Workers Union, have walked off the job in protest over wage negotiations and working conditions, demanding a 15% salary hike and enhanced safety measures.

Manufacturing sites in Pune, Chennai, and Vadodara—key centers for the industry—have been particularly impacted, with assembly lines at firms such as Eastern Switchgear Ltd and Sunvolt Electricals Pvt Ltd standing idle. Factory gates remained locked on Tuesday, and company officials confirmed that production schedules are now facing significant delays.

“Negotiations have stalled. Without management’s commitment to improved compensation and safer workplaces, our members have no choice but to continue the strike,” said Pramod Sharma, general secretary of the union. He estimated over 18,000 workers are currently participating in the action.

Industry analysts warn that ongoing disruptions could affect order backlogs and delivery timelines. “A protracted shutdown will make it challenging for manufacturers to fulfill existing contracts and may lead to financial pressure,” said Kavita Desai, an analyst with Mumbai-based research firm Zenith Markets.

Managers at Westindia Electrical Components Ltd reported that their Vadodara plant, which produces circuit breakers and distribution panels, has ceased operations entirely since Monday morning. “We are hopeful for a swift resolution, but at present, our facilities remain closed,” said a company spokesperson.

The Electrical Equipment Manufacturers Association of India has urged both sides to return to the negotiating table. “It is imperative that an agreement be reached to restore normalcy and safeguard the interests of both workers and companies,” said Association President Rajeev Patil.

Talks are scheduled to resume later this week.
